page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-24 is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 24 dedicated virtual CPUs and 90.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The c4n-standard-24 instance provides a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources, positioning it within the general-purpose and compute-adjacent hardware classes. Because it lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O or hardware-accelerated parallel processing must attach external block storage or select alternative instance families. This resource density offers a predictable cost-efficiency profile for workloads that rely strictly on dedicated CPU execution and moderate memory capacity without the overhead of unused local hardware.

This server configuration is designed for workloads such as web serving, application hosting, containerized microservices, and general-purpose business logic. The 24 dedicated vCPUs provide parallel processing capacity for multi-threaded applications, while the 90.0 GB of RAM supports moderate database caching and memory-resident application runtimes.
